root_cause.text: The kl5kusb105 USB-serial driver’s `klsi_105_prepare_write_buffer()` copied up to the full 64-byte bulk-out buffer into `buf + KLSI_HDR_LEN` while also reserving the first 2 bytes for a length header, causing a 2-byte slab out-of-bounds write when the write FIFO contained at least `size` bytes.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `kfifo_out_locked(&port->write_fifo, buf + KLSI_HDR_LEN, size, &port->lock);` to `size - KLSI_HDR_LEN`, and the CVE description states the function “stores a two-byte length header at the start of the buffer” but “passes the full buffer size as the number of bytes to copy,” resulting in “writing KLSI_HDR_LEN bytes past its end.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix the KLSI 105 write buffer preparation to account for the protocol header when sizing the payload copy.
intent_record.what: In klsi_105_prepare_write_buffer(), the kfifo_out_locked() call was changed so its third argument is now `size - KLSI_HDR_LEN` instead of `size`, and the line was rewrapped for formatting.
intent_record.how: The function now limits the amount of FIFO data copied into the payload area to the buffer space remaining after reserving room for the protocol header, preventing the write data from overrunning the destination buffer and keeping the returned total length consistent with the header plus payload.

grouping_result.intent: Fix the KLSI 105 write buffer preparation to account for the protocol header when sizing the payload copy.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it fixes klsi_105_prepare_write_buffer() to account for the 2-byte protocol header when copying the payload, which prevents the described out-of-bounds write.

candidates.rationale: This copy operation writes payload bytes starting at buf + KLSI_HDR_LEN while still using size as the maximum payload length, so if size equals the full buffer size it overflows the 2-byte header reservation and can write past the end of the slab object.

This stores the length header into the beginning of the same buffer; combined with the oversized payload copy above, it reflects the protocol layout that reserved header space but did not reduce the payload copy limit.

vuln_statements.explanation: This copies payload data starting at buf + KLSI_HDR_LEN while still allowing up to size bytes, which can overrun the 2-byte header reservation when size is the full bulk-out buffer length, causing the slab out-of-bounds write.

This writes the protocol length header into the first bytes of the same buffer, confirming the layout mismatch: header space was reserved but the payload copy limit was not reduced accordingly, enabling the overflow.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct is not present in this commit. The old custom write path that copied payload into the bulk-out buffer is completely removed: the diff deletes `klsi_105_write()` and its logic, including `memcpy(urb->transfer_buffer + KLSI_105_DATA_OFFSET, buf, size);` and the 64-byte buffer handling. The new write path is `klsi_105_prepare_write_buffer()`, which uses `kfifo_out_locked(&port->write_fifo, buf + KLSI_HDR_LEN, size, &port->lock);` and then writes the header with `put_unaligned_le16(count, buf);`. This still reserves 2 bytes for the header (`KLSI_HDR_LEN`), so the prior out-of-bounds write condition is no longer present. Therefore `has_bug=false` and `is_fixed=true`.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct described in the root cause is the custom write-buffer packing that copied payload into a 64-byte bulk-out buffer while reserving the first 2 bytes for a header. In this commit, that entire custom write path is removed: the old `klsi_105_write()` with `size = min(count, port->bulk_out_size - KLSI_105_DATA_OFFSET);` and `memcpy(urb->transfer_buffer + KLSI_105_DATA_OFFSET, buf, size);` no longer exists. Since the buggy construct is absent and the fix is already present, `has_bug` is false and `is_fixed` is true.
